# fgls

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/emiliogcs/fgls/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/emiliogcs/fgls/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**fgls** estimates linear regressions by feasible generalized least squares
when the errors are serially correlated, heteroskedastic of unknown form, or
both:

* **Serial correlation** (Perron and González-Coya, 2026). An AR filter is
  estimated from a Durbin regression, with its order chosen by BIC. This is
  consistent when the regressors are only *pre-determined* (they react to past
  shocks), where OLS and Cochrane-Orcutt are not. A variance estimator accounts
  for the estimated filter.
* **Heteroskedasticity of unknown form** (González-Coya and Perron, 2024). An
  adaptive Lasso of the log squared residuals on candidate covariates gives the
  weights, and a bias-corrected sandwich variance keeps inference valid when the
  variance model is wrong. If nothing is selected, FGLS equals OLS.
* **Both together** (Supplement S-4 of the 2026 paper).

It is the R counterpart of the Python package
[pyfgls](https://pypi.org/project/pyfgls/), and agrees with it to machine
precision on deterministic quantities. More code by the author:
<https://emiliogcs.com/code/>.

## Installation

```r
# development version
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("emiliogcs/fgls")
# from CRAN, once released
install.packages("fgls")
```

## Serial correlation with a non-exogenous regressor

```{r serial}
library(fgls)
sim <- simulate_serial(500, seed = 1) # design of Table 1 of the 2026 paper; true slope 1
fit <- serial_fgls(y ~ x, data = sim)
summary(fit)
compare_fgls(OLS = lm(y ~ x, data = sim), FGLS = fit)
```

## Heteroskedasticity of unknown form

```{r hetero}
het <- simulate_hetero(200, skedastic = "log2", seed = 2)
fit_h <- lasso_fgls(y ~ x, data = het, seed = 1)
fit_h$skedastic$selected
compare_fgls(OLS = lm(y ~ x, data = het), FGLS = fit_h)
```

## Both

```{r both}
both <- simulate_combined(200, ar = 0.5, skedastic = "x2", seed = 3)
fit_b <- fgls(y ~ x, data = both, seed = 1)
fit_b
```

See `vignette("fgls")` to get started, and the articles on
[serial correlation](https://emiliogcs.com/fgls/articles/serial-correlation.html),
[heteroskedasticity](https://emiliogcs.com/fgls/articles/heteroskedasticity.html),
the [combined estimator](https://emiliogcs.com/fgls/articles/combined.html) and the
[validation](https://emiliogcs.com/fgls/articles/validation.html) against the papers
and pyfgls.
